draft.title: Conditional statements
card: A conditional statement has the form if P then Q. P is the condition and Q is the result. It makes a promise: whenever P is true, Q is true too.
The promise is broken in only one case: P is true and Q is false. In every other case the statement is true, including when P is false.
The contrapositive of if P then Q is if not Q then not P. It is true in exactly the same cases, so it means the same as the original.
Example: if a number ends in 0, then it is divisible by 5. The contrapositive is: if a number is not divisible by 5, then it does not end in 0. Both are true.
draft.remember: If P then Q fails only when P is true and Q is false. The contrapositive says the same thing.

a.q: Ravi says: if it rains, then the match is cancelled. It rains, but the match goes ahead. Is Ravi's statement true or false?
opts: False, because P is true and Q is false
True, because the match was not cancelled
True, because the statement only needs P to be true
False, because it is not always raining
a.why: The only way if P then Q fails is P true and Q false. Here it rained and the match was not cancelled, so the statement is false. Saying it is true because the match went ahead ignores the promise that rain leads to cancellation.
a.clue: Check whether the promise was broken when P happened.

b.q: Which is the contrapositive of: if a shape is a square, then it has four equal sides?
opts: If not four equal sides, then not a square
If four equal sides, then a square
If not a square, then not four equal sides
If a square, then not four equal sides
b.why: The contrapositive swaps P and Q and negates both: if not Q then not P. So not having four equal sides leads to not being a square. The second option swaps but does not negate, and the third negates but does not swap, so neither means the same as the original.
b.clue: Swap the two parts and put not on both.

a.best: False, because P is true and Q is false

b.best: If not four equal sides, then not a square

problems.detail: The why names wrong options by position ('the second option swaps but does not negate, and the third negates but does not swap'), but options are shown in random order. Even in the order given the labels do not match: the converse is listed first and the inverse second. Students reading the why would be pointed to the wrong options. Describe them by content instead, e.g. 'If four equal sides, then a square' swaps but does not negate.

check.summary: The card and both questions are correct and each has one clear right answer. The why for (b) names the wrong options by position, which will not match the shuffled order, so it should name them by their wording instead.
